QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_25

question.text: What happens to the margin account when a futures position is marked-to-market daily?

answer.text: If the position moves favorably, the margin account is credited; if it moves adversely, the account is debited — any notional loss must be deposited within the stipulated time, or the broker may liquidate the position
The margin account remains constant regardless of price movements
The margin account only changes at contract expiry
The margin account is credited daily regardless of price direction as a reward for holding the position

explanation.text: The Logic: Daily mark-to-market: gains are paid to the gainer and losses are collected from the loss-making participant via debits to the margin account. If a position moves unfavourably, the resulting notional loss must be deposited within the stipulated time; failure to do so allows the broker to liquidate the position. The Trap: Margin accounts change daily, not just at expiry, and they are not credited unconditionally — credits and debits depend on the direction of price movement. Note: The source-backed trigger here is the requirement to deposit the notional loss within the stipulated time and the broker's right to liquidate on failure; a separate maintenance-margin trigger was not found in the pages checked.
